options: It never reaches a terminal state
It is guaranteed to reach a terminal state after a finite number of steps, then resets
It requires γ < 1 to be well-defined
It only has one possible action at each state
questions.explain: Episodic tasks reach a special terminal state after finitely many steps (e.g. checkmate, reaching a maze exit), after which the environment resets for a new episode.

questions.q: Why do continuing tasks require γ < 1 for the return to be well-defined?
options: Because continuing tasks have no reward function
Because the return is an infinite sum, and γ < 1 with bounded rewards is needed for that sum to converge to a finite number
Because continuing tasks always have negative rewards
Because γ only matters for episodic tasks
questions.explain: G_t = Σ γ^k R_{t+k+1} is an infinite sum for a continuing task. Without γ < 1 (and bounded rewards), that sum can diverge to infinity.

questions.q: In Gymnasium's step() return value, what does terminated=True signal?
options: The episode was cut off by an external time limit
The episode ended because the agent reached a genuine terminal state defined by the task itself
The environment crashed
The agent's action was invalid
questions.explain: terminated=True indicates a 'real' ending defined by the task's own dynamics, such as the pole falling in CartPole — distinct from an externally imposed cutoff.

questions.q: What does truncated=True typically indicate in Gymnasium?
options: The agent achieved the maximum possible reward
The episode was cut off for an external reason, most commonly a time limit, even though the task could have continued
The transition function P changed mid-episode
The reward function was reset to zero
questions.explain: truncated=True means the episode ended for a reason outside the task's own dynamics — typically a step limit like CartPole-v1's 500-step cap — not because a genuine terminal state was reached.

questions.q: Why shouldn't a truncated step be bootstrapped the same way as a terminated step when estimating value functions?
options: Truncated steps always have zero reward
A truncated episode's next state still has real future value, unlike a genuinely terminated state which has none
Bootstrapping is never used with truncated episodes
truncated and terminated are functionally identical and can always be treated the same
questions.explain: A terminated state has, by definition, no future value to bootstrap from. A truncated state was cut off artificially and still has real future value that a correct implementation should account for.
